Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Raj Singh, CFO; Dr. Priya Mehta, CTO; and Tom Reilly, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results may differ materially due to a variety of factors. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q and 10-K, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge Inc.'s performance for Q3 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge AI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives across enterprise DevOps, analytics, and workflow automation.

Our focus this quarter was on five key areas: capital allocation, new customer acquisition, ARR growth, free cash flow, and operating expense breakdown.

Starting with capital allocation, which remains a cornerstone of our disciplined approach to driving long-term shareholder value in the SaaS landscape. At CloudForge, we operate with a robust $2.8 billion in cash and equivalents as of quarter end, bolstered by strong free cash flow generation of $450 million over the past four quarters, representing 28% FCF margins on $1.6 billion of ARR at that point. Our leverage is minimal at 0.8x net debt to EBITDA, giving us significant dry powder to execute flexibly across organic investments, tuck-in M&A, and opportunistic returns to shareholders.

Our philosophy is straightforward: prioritize high-ROI opportunities that accelerate our Rule of 40 trajectory, currently at 48% with 32% YoY ARR growth and 16% expansion in dollar-based net retention, or NRR. We target deployments yielding at least 20% IRR on incremental capital, benchmarked against peers like Salesforce and ServiceNow. In FY24, we allocated $650 million of capital, up 15% YoY, with 55% to organic growth initiatives, 30% to M&A, and 15% to share repurchases.

First, organic investments are our highest priority. We've committed $350 million this year to R&D and go-to-market, representing 22% of revenue. On the product side, $180 million is fueling AI-native enhancements to our core CRM and analytics platform, CloudForge One. This includes embedding generative AI capabilities similar to Salesforce's Einstein or Adobe's Firefly, such as predictive lead scoring powered by fine-tuned LLMs from partners like Anthropic and our own proprietary models trained on 10 petabytes of anonymized customer data. Early wins show beta users reporting 35% faster pipeline velocity, contributing to our 125% NRR in AI upsell cohorts.

Regionally, we're doubling down on APAC, where ARR grew 55% YoY to $220 million, driven by demand for compliant, low-latency SaaS amid digital sovereignty regulations like India's DPDP Act. $50 million is earmarked for Tokyo and Singapore data centers with sovereign cloud integrations, partnering with AWS Outposts for edge processing, as we target the $150 billion APAC SaaS TAM by 2028 per Gartner. In EMEA, $40 million supports GDPR Phase 3 upgrades and zero-trust architecture, maintaining 18% growth versus the street's 12% for the region.

Sales and marketing receives $120 million, focused on mid-market expansion via our CloudForge Flex tier, priced at $50 per user per month with usage-based metering. This has driven 40% of new logo ACV from SMBs, with CAC payback now at 14 months, down from 18, thanks to AI-optimized inside sales funnels.

Second, M&A remains targeted and accretive. We've executed three deals totaling $200 million YTD, all cash, with immediate 10-15% ARR accretion. The standout was our $120 million acquisition of DataForge AI in Q2, a Tel Aviv-based startup with a composable analytics engine that integrates seamlessly with Snowflake and Databricks. This bolsters our data moat, adding 15,000 customers and $45 million in ARR at 112% NRR, while accelerating time-to-market for our Multimodal Insights module amid the 60% YoY surge in enterprise AI spend, as noted in Bessemer's Cloud Index.

We also acquired SecureLink, a $40 million bootstrapper offering API gateway security, for $30 million, timely given rising ransomware threats where 25% of breaches now target SaaS supply chains per CrowdStrike reports. In APAC, our $25 million purchase of Syncra Pte enhances our Singapore hub with real-time collaboration tools for SEA fintechs, projecting 25% revenue synergies. Our pipeline has 10-12 tuck-ins under LOI, focusing on vertical SaaS in healthcare with HIPAA-compliant workflows and cybersecurity adjacencies, steering clear of 2021's frothy valuations. We expect $250-300 million in FY25 M&A, financed 70% cash and 30% stock to preserve our 85% gross margins.

Finally, returns to shareholders: With our valuation at 8x EV/FCF, attractive versus the SaaS index at 12x, we repurchased $100 million in shares YTD, retiring 2.5 million shares or 1.8% of float at an average $145 per share. This is opportunistic; we'll scale to $200 million annually if multiples compress further amid high rates. No dividends yet, as we're growth-first like Snowflake, but we'll revisit post-35% FCF margins.

Looking ahead, Q4 capex guidance is $80-90 million, skewed to AI infra, with FY25 total deployment at $700-800 million assuming stable macro. Our balance sheet strength, including a $1.2 billion undrawn revolver, positions us to weather SaaS winter while outpacing peers. Risks include FX volatility in APAC, with 5% ARR exposure hedged, and AI capex inflation, but our 95% gross retention and land-and-expand flywheel de-risk this.

Moving to new customer acquisition, which continues to be a cornerstone of our growth story. In this quarter, Q3 FY2024, we onboarded 1,450 new customers, a robust 38% year-over-year increase from the 1,050 added in Q3 FY2023, and a sequential uptick of 12% from Q2's 1,295.

These new logos contributed $22.4 million in new ARR, representing approximately 32% of our total ARR expansion for the quarter. Our ending ARR now stands at $512 million, up 45% YoY, with new customer ARR driving a 28% quarter-over-quarter lift in MRR. We closed the quarter at $42.7 million MRR, reflecting the compounding power of our multi-tiered go-to-market strategy.

Breaking it down by segments, this highlights our diversification away from pure SMB dependency:

- SMB/Self-Serve under $10K ARR: 1,120 customers added, up 52% YoY, fueled by PLG enhancements. Average new ARR per customer was $4.2K, with conversion from free tier to paid at a record 18%, 300 basis points above LTM average. Key driver is our Forge Lite self-serve plan, integrated with Slack, Microsoft Teams, and Google Workspace, reducing time-to-value to under 5 minutes, mirroring Notion or Linear's viral playbook.

- Mid-Market $10K-$100K ARR: 210 new customers, flat YoY but with 22% higher average ARR at $45K per customer. Inside sales teams used ABM targeting fintech and e-commerce, leveraging intent data from 6sense.

- Enterprise over $100K ARR: 120 new customers, surging 75% YoY, adding $14.8 million in new ARR at an average $123K per deal. Wins include a top-5 global bank for AI-powered real-time fraud detection and two Fortune 500 retailers adopting our data orchestration post-45-day POCs. This segment shows 145% dollar-based net expansion rate in the first 12 months.

Regionally:

North America: 785 new customers, 54% of total, +25% YoY, $12.1M new ARR.

EMEA: 385, 27%, +55% YoY, $6.2M.

APAC: 280, 19%, +62% YoY, $4.1M.

EMEA accelerated via our Dublin hub and GDPR features closing DAX 40 deals. APAC via Singapore office and AWS Marketplace, Snowflake partnerships, with 40% of adds from channels and 2x global TCV.

This is high-quality acquisition: CAC payback at 11 months from 14 last year, 35% new ARR from inbound leads up from 22%, driven by content like our 'State of AI Analytics' webinars generating 50+ SQLs. API-first extensibility with Databricks and dbt boosted RFP win rates 22%.

Ahead, Q4 guidance implies 1,600+ new customers and $28M+ new ARR, lapping industry 25% median per Bessemer. With 92% gross retention and 118% NRR, and enterprise pipeline up 65% YoY at $1.2B ACV, AI tailwinds accelerate us.

Next, ARR growth. For Q3 FY2024, total ARR stands at $512 million, up an impressive 45% year-over-year from last year, and 28% quarter-over-quarter from Q2. These figures beat guidance and position us at the high end of SaaS peers, outpacing median 22% YoY amid macro headwinds.

YoY growth driven by new ACV contributing heavily, with 1,450 net new logos including seven-figure hyperscaler and financial deals. NRR at 118%, strong in enterprise with expansions like e-commerce platforms adding 30% footprint.

QoQ 28% acceleration from seasonality and Q2-launched AI-Optimized Release Engine, automating CI/CD bottlenecks like GitHub Copilot, with 75% pilot conversions adding  points to growth. Multi-year contracts now 65% of nACV smooth expansions, countering SMB churn as we prioritize higher-LTV.

U.S. 31% YoY to dominant share, EMEA 25% to strong regulated verticals, APAC 42% standout with Japan/India wins and Kubernetes integrations.

This validates our platform flywheel: land with pipeline tools, expand to security, AI testing, governance. R&D up 15% YoY for GitOps, zero-trust DevSecOps, $15B TAM by 2027 per Aberdeen. Q4 YoY ARR growth 27-30%, sequential 7-9%, with sales ramp and Federated Multi-Cloud GA.

With 98% gross retention, NRR >110% for eight quarters, Rule of 55 at 68, we're set for compounding despite macro scrutiny like at Snowflake.

Turning to free cash flow. For Q3, we generated $52 million in free cash flow, a 28% year-over-year increase from $40.6 million last year. This is our 11th straight positive quarter, with YTD $118 million up 42%. Q3 FCF margin at 22% vs. 18% YoY, on track for full-year $240-260 million, 30-35% growth.

Operating cash flow $58 million up 32% YoY, CapEx disciplined at $6 million or 2.5% revenue, leveraging AWS/Azure.

Drivers: Revenue up 32% to $168 million, ARR $512 million up 45%, NRR 118% from AI upsells, 45% new bookings >$1M ARR, 95% gross retention.

Working capital: DSO 62 days from 68, $15M deferred unwind reduction, adding $22M OCF.

Margins: Non-GAAP op margins 28% from 24%, gross 83%, CAC payback 14 months from 17 via inside sales, partners like Accenture. R&D up 15% offset by 20% productivity.

Broad-based: North America $42M up 35%, EMEA $8M up 50%, APAC $2M up 15%, accelerating with Singapore DC.

Rule of 40 at 52, $75M YTD repurchases at $85/share, 65% FCF returned, dry powder for M&A like recent predictive analytics tuck-in, LTV/CAC >5x.

H2 acceleration from large deals, efficiencies like AWS reserved instances. Risks: sales cycles, but expansions buffer. 25%+ FCF growth into FY25 with AI.

Finally, operating expense breakdown. Total non-GAAP op ex $128 million, up 12% YoY but flat QoQ, 85% of $150 million revenue prior context, improving margin 400bps to 15%. Rule of 40 at 48 with 28% growth, 125% NRR.

R&D $42 million, 28% revenue, up 18% YoY, down from Q1. Strategic for GenAI in CloudForge Orchestrate, agentic AI for code gen, predictive analytics, 35% QoQ upsell in top 500.

60% US Seattle/Austin, 45 engineers for low-code, zero-trust, GDPR/SEC. EMEA Dublin 12-person for multilingual LLMs, +15% win rates vs. UiPath. APAC Singapore for fintech. Headcount +8% to 620, productivity +22% via Copilot-like, peak 29% Q3 then 26-27%.

Sales & Marketing $68 million, 45% revenue, up 10% YoY, down 5% QoQ. Efficiency focus, CAC payback 14 months. 20% ramp enterprise, 18 >$1M deals incl. $5M Fortune 50 bank.

PLG shift: inbound 55% pipeline, freemium Accelerate $12M new ARR, CAC $8K. Content ROI 3.5x, paid search -15%. US 65%, EMEA +25% to $17M sovereign cloud, APAC $10M AWS/Azure channels. Sales headcount flat 450, quotas +15%, magic number 1.25 like Datadog. To 42-43% year-end.

G&A $18 million, 12% revenue, flat YoY/QoQ from 13.5%. $6M people, no net adds post-10% optimization like Workday. SBC 2.5%, fees +5% SOX, facilities -8% hybrid Bellevue HQ. Intl 20%, NIS2/DPDP compliance. To 10-11% long-term >$700M ARR.

This OpEx balances innovation, growth, stability, FY24 guidance $520-530M intact.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Raj Singh to discuss the financials in more detail.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $168 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 83%, and operating income was $42 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $2.8 billion, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first three quarters of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $680 million to $700 million, with ARR ending the year around $580-600 million.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Priya Mehta for a technology update.

Dr. Priya Mehta:
Thank you, Raj. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. Our CloudForge AI platform, with generative AI for predictive analytics, automated DevOps, and multimodal insights, is seeing strong adoption, driving increased user engagement—up 35% in beta cohorts—and improved customer outcomes like 2x faster release cycles.

We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability, rolling out zero-trust architecture compliant with GDPR Phase 3, NIS2, and DPDP, plus sovereign cloud options via AWS Outposts. This supports our enterprise customers' growing demands, with integrations to Snowflake, Databricks, and dbt reducing time-to-value. Our R&D investments are positioning us ahead in GitOps, DevSecOps, and agentic AI, targeting the $15B TAM. Early pilots show 75% conversion, fueling NRR above 120% in AI users.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge AI on your overall growth, and what kind of attach rates are you seeing with it?

Tom Reilly:
Thanks, Emily. The CloudForge AI platform has been transformative for our growth, contributing roughly 25% of new ARR this quarter through upsells and new logos. Enterprise customers expanding from core modules to AI features like predictive lead scoring and automated workflows saw 125% NRR in those cohorts, accelerating pipeline velocity by 35%. Attach rates are strong at 65% among existing customers trialing it, with 75% converting to paid post-pilot. In new deals, it's bundling at 55%, driving average ACV up 22% to $123K in enterprise. This mirrors Einstein's impact at Salesforce, and with our 10PB data moat, we're seeing 40% of APAC wins include AI from day one. Happy to dive deeper.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lopez with JPMorgan.

David Lopez:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, David. APAC is a priority, with ARR up 55-62% YoY to $220 million, fastest growing region. We're investing $50 million in Tokyo and Singapore data centers with AWS Outposts for low-latency, sovereign compliance amid DPDP and similar regs. Partnerships via AWS Marketplace, Snowflake Data Cloud, and local channels drove 280 new customers this quarter, 19% of total but 18% of new ARR. Singapore hub enhancements from Syncra acquisition target SEA fintechs with real-time tools. Sales ramp to 25 reps in Dublin supports EMEA spillover, but APAC pipeline is up 65% at $250M ACV, chasing Gartner's $150B TAM by 2028. Multi-year commitments here average 2x global TCV. We'll deploy $100 million+ FY25 for localization, Kubernetes-native features.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays.

Rachel Kim:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, and what's the trend you are seeing in NRR?

Raj Singh:
Great question, Rachel. Churn remains low at under 8% gross, with 92-98% gross retention despite macro pressures like high rates and scrutiny. We're managing it through land-and-expand, prioritizing high-LTV enterprise—de-emphasizing low-ACV SMB—and AI upsells yielding 125-145% NRR in cohorts. Overall dollar-based NRR steady at 118% for eight quarters, above 110% consistently, with expansions offsetting any contraction. Enterprise cohort first-year DBNER at 145%, driven by multi-year deals at 65% of nACV. Inbound-led efficiency (35% new ARR) and PLG keep CAC payback at 11-14 months. Trends improving with AI adoption; Q4 expect NRR 119-120% as pilots convert. Our flywheel and 95% retention de-risk economic uncertainty.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Capital allocation: Discuss capital allocation strategy (investments, acquisitions, etc.).
New customer acquisition: Number of new customers added, and impact on ARR/MRR.

Plans $250-300M FY25 M&A, Q4 capex $80-90M.

Diversified across SMB (1,120), mid-market (210), enterprise (120); NA/EMEA/APAC splits.
